title: Fluke vs Augury: Condition Monitoring Compared (2027) | Tractian
summary: Fluke vs Augury for condition monitoring: compare sensors, who diagnoses alerts, hazardous-area ratings, CMMS integration and pricing, plus a third option.
body_markdown:
## Key Points


- Fluke sells each part of a monitoring program separately, while Augury sells them together in one subscription.
- Compare who diagnoses each alert, how sensor data leaves the plant, and which hazardous-area certificates the sensors carry.
- Tractian adds a third choice: one wireless sensor per asset, AI that names the fault, and integrations with the CMMS you already run.


Fluke vs Augury comes down to how each company packages condition monitoring. Fluke Reliability sells a toolbox of portable instruments, wireless vibration sensors, analyst services and the eMaint CMMS, and a plant can mix those parts. Augury sells a monitoring subscription in which its sensors, AI diagnostics and vibration analysts come as one service.


That difference makes the two quotes hard to line up. This guide compares them on signals, diagnosis, deployment, hazardous-area coverage and CMMS integration, then shows where a third option, Tractian, fits. Plants weighing more vendors can compare[Fluke alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/fluke-alternatives) and[Augury alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/augury-alternatives) .


## Fluke vs Augury at a glance


Fluke offers separate instruments, sensors, software and services under one brand, while Augury offers a single subscription built around its own sensors.


Feature Fluke Augury


Product family Fluke Reliability: Azima wireless sensors and analyst services, eMaint CMMS, portable test and alignment tools Augury machine health platform with its own sensors, portable device and services


Sensors and signals Accel 310 wireless sensors measuring triaxial vibration Halo sensors measuring triaxial vibration, temperature and magnetic flux; ultrasonic sensor for slow-speed machines


Handheld or portable tools Thermal cameras, acoustic imagers, laser alignment and vibration products sold as separate instruments Auguscope portable sensing device for route-based checks, with results in the Augury platform


Where analysis runs WATCHMAN analytics software turns sensor data into fault diagnoses and repair recommendations AI diagnostics in the Augury platform


Who reviews alerts Automated diagnosis, plus human review by certified analysts as a second opinion Automated diagnosis, plus human review by vibration analysts


Connectivity Contact vendor for current details Wireless sensors report through Augury gateways; the slow-speed hub sends data over Wi-Fi or cellular


Hazardous-area ratings Accel 310 sensors described as IP and EX rated; zone details from the vendor Separate hazardous-area sensor with ATEX, IECEx and CSA approvals


CMMS integration eMaint CMMS from Fluke Reliability, which also lists ERP and IIoT integrations Automated work orders into CMMS and EAM systems such as SAP, IBM Maximo and MaintainX

## Fluke Reliability: tools, sensors and software


Under the Fluke Reliability name, Fluke combines portable test instruments, Azima wireless vibration sensors, remote analyst services and the eMaint CMMS. Its continuous monitoring sensors and analyst services are sold under the Azima name.


### Key features


- Wireless sensors: Azima Accel 310 sensors mount on the asset and record triaxial vibration, with a stated battery life of 3 years.
- **Diagnostics:** WATCHMAN analytics software converts the readings into fault diagnoses and repair recommendations, with hourly summaries and a daily diagnostic run.
- **Analyst services:** Remote analysts provide a second opinion on the data and vibration analysis when requested.
- **Maintenance software:** eMaint is Fluke Reliability's CMMS, and its condition monitoring module connects Fluke sensors to work orders.
- **Portable instruments:** Fluke also sells thermal cameras, acoustic imagers, laser alignment tools and vibration products as standalone instruments.


### Where Fluke fits


Fluke fits plants that already run route-based inspections with Fluke instruments and want to add wireless sensors and remote analysis. Fluke sensor alarms can trigger work orders in eMaint, the Fluke Reliability CMMS.


### How much does Fluke cost?


Fluke Reliability quotes wireless monitoring and eMaint plans through its sales team rather than a published list.


### Questions to ask Fluke before you buy


- Which wireless sensor line replaces the 3563 system, now listed as discontinued?
- Which hazardous-area zones does the Accel 310 certificate cover?
- How does sensor data reach the cloud from a plant without open Wi-Fi?
- Which alerts reach a human analyst, and how fast?
- How many setup steps does eMaint need before alerts open work orders?
- Can the sensors send alerts to a CMMS other than eMaint?


## Augury: subscription services with sensors


Augury sells continuous machine health monitoring as a subscription that includes its sensors, AI diagnostics and support from vibration analysts. Coverage is split into standard, low RPM and hazardous-area sensor families, plus a portable device for route checks.


### Key features


- **Standard sensors:** Halo sensors read magnetic flux, temperature and vibration on three axes, with IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings and a field-replaceable battery.
- **Classified zones:** Augury offers a different sensor model for Class I/II, Division 1/2 hazardous areas, with ATEX, IECEx and CSA approvals.
- **Diagnosis:** AI names the fault and its likely cause, with vibration analysts behind the prescriptive guidance.
- **Portable checks:** the Auguscope device collects route readings that land in the same platform as sensor data.
- **Work orders:** integrations send fault, severity and recommended action into CMMS and EAM systems, including SAP, IBM Maximo and MaintainX.


### Where Augury fits


Augury suits plants that prefer to buy sensors, diagnosis and analyst support under one contract, with Augury hardware on each monitored machine.


### How is Augury priced?


Augury gives a quote after the demo and keeps no public price list.


### Questions to ask Augury before you buy


- Does the platform work with data from sensors already installed, or does it depend on[proprietary Augury hardware](https://www.g2.com/products/augury/reviews/augury-review-13567122) ?
- How many[alerts in the first months turn out to be minor or not actionable](https://www.g2.com/products/augury/reviews/augury-review-13781259) , and how long does it take to cut that noise?
- When a CMMS setup needs[custom mapping](https://www.g2.com/products/augury/reviews/augury-review-13780950) , how often do automated handoffs stall and leave planners to bridge the gap by hand?
- Which assets need a gateway, and where must it be mounted?
- Can reports and raw data be exported without manual rework?
- What happens to the sensors if the subscription ends?


## Fluke or Augury: which fits your plant?


Pick by the gap you need to close: Fluke suits plants building on an instrument and CMMS stack, while Augury suits plants that want monitoring bought as one service.


Plant situation What to look for Fluke offer Augury offer


Route program with trained analysts Route readings and sensor data in one asset history Portable instruments plus Azima sensors, with eMaint as the maintenance record Auguscope readings stored in the same platform as continuous sensor data


No vibration analyst on staff Automated fault names, severity and a repair step, with human review on hard calls WATCHMAN diagnoses plus a second opinion from certified analysts AI diagnostics with vibration analysts behind the recommendations


Remote assets or a locked-down plant network How sensor data leaves the plant, and whether plant IT has to approve a new device Contact vendor for current details Gateways for standard sensors; Wi-Fi or cellular for the slow-speed hub


Classified areas (Class I Div 1, ATEX zones) A certificate that matches the zone where each sensor will sit EX-rated Accel 310 sensors; confirm the zone with Fluke A separate hazardous-area sensor family


Slow-speed assets such as kilns and rotary drums Low-RPM fault detection and sampling that fits long rotation periods Contact vendor for current details Ultrasonic sensor for machines turning as slow as 1 RPM


An existing CMMS other than the vendor's own Alerts that open a work order with the fault, severity and recommended action eMaint integrations; check the connector for your CMMS Work order integrations with several CMMS and EAM platforms


Whichever way the table points, run the trial on two or three assets with a known failure history, such as a cooling tower fan gearbox or a process pump with repeat bearing changes. Compare how early each system flags the fault, what the alert tells the technician, and how long the work order takes to appear.[Handheld analyzers versus continuous monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/blog/handheld-vibration-analyzer-or-continuous-monitoring) covers how routes and sensors split the work.

### How Tractian detects and diagnoses faults


Each critical machine gets its own[Smart Trac Ultra](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/ultrasonic-sensor) , which records vibration, continuous ultrasound, temperature and RPM on that asset with a sampling rate as high as 64 kHz. The ultrasound channel hears bearing friction from poor lubrication, so a technician can grease on condition and see the signal drop as the grease goes in.


[Auto Diagnosis](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/auto-diagnosis) turns the readings into a named failure mode, for example an outer race defect, a misaligned coupling or an unbalanced fan. Each call is checked against a large history of machine data, and the alert lists severity, asset criticality, the probable root cause and the repair steps. Learn more about[vibration analysis in Tractian](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/vibration-analysis) .


On motors where electrical faults are the bigger risk,[Energy Trac](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/energy-trac) adds current, voltage and power factor data, and its fault list covers rotor, stator, winding and insulation problems as well as voltage imbalance.


Smart Trac Ultra on the machine and Energy Trac in the electrical panel that feeds its motor together form[multimodal monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/multimodal) , and Janus, Tractian’s industrial AI trained on proprietary data from real machines, reads the mechanical and electrical signals as one picture of asset health.

- Quick install: the wireless sensor is glued or screwed to the machine in minutes, and its battery lasts up to 5 years.
- **No Wi-Fi required:** data travels over 4G/LTE, so plant IT does not have to open Wi-Fi or run cable for it.
- **Hazardous and washdown areas:** the IP69K housing is[Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) .
- **Integrations:** Tractian[integrations](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) send alerts and asset data to popular CMMS platforms such as MaintainX, Fiix, UpKeep and Limble, and to ERPs such as SAP and Oracle NetSuite. An API also links Tractian to SCADA and APM systems, so the data reaches the tools a plant already uses.
- **Custom reporting:** Power BI and SQL connectors let teams build their own dashboards and reports on downtime, failure trends and costs.
- **Time to value:** most Tractian customers reach full operation within 14 days, while the sensors learn how each machine normally runs.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the main difference between Fluke and Augury for condition monitoring?


Fluke Reliability sells a portfolio of handheld test tools, wireless sensors, remote analysis and its own CMMS, and plants can buy each part separately. Augury sells a machine health subscription that bundles its sensors, AI diagnostics and analyst support. The practical difference shows up in the quote, in who owns the diagnosis, and in how alerts reach your work order system.


### Do wireless vibration sensors replace handheld vibration routes?


Sensors take over the routine readings on the assets they are mounted on, so technicians stop walking those points on a schedule. Handheld tools still earn their place for post-repair checks, balancing and alignment jobs, and assets that are not yet instrumented. Many plants run both and shorten the routes as sensor coverage grows.


### Who should review condition monitoring alerts?


Software can name common faults, such as a worn bearing, a misaligned shaft or an unbalanced rotor, and rank them by severity. A reliability engineer or vibration analyst should still look at alerts on critical assets before a planned shutdown is booked. Tractian pairs automated diagnosis with expert-vetted human review when a call needs a second look.


### Can wireless condition monitoring sensors be used in hazardous areas?


Yes, if the sensor carries a certificate for the zone where it is installed, such as ATEX or IECEx for Zone ratings or Class I Division 1 in North America. Ask for the certificate itself, not a datasheet line, and check it against your area classification drawing. Tractian sensors are Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant.


### How do condition monitoring alerts turn into work orders?


The monitoring platform either creates the work order itself or pushes the alert into the CMMS through an integration. A useful work order carries the asset, the fault, its severity and the recommended action, so the planner does not have to open a second system. Ask each vendor to show the handoff live with your CMMS during the trial.
